real_qa.q: How should contractors match their follow-up approach to different lead sources based on customer intent levels?
real_qa.r: Different marketing channels attract different levels of intent. Facebook leads score 3 out of 10 intent and need instant automated text and email, multiple touches over time, and helpful educational content. Google search leads score 8 out of 10 and need an immediate phone call and direct path to booking. Door knocking scores 1 out of 10 and needs patience, while referrals score 9 out of 10 and need appreciation. Matching your approach to the lead source dramatically improves conversion rates.

real_qa.q: What specific steps should contractors follow during an estimate walkthrough to build trust with customers?
real_qa.r: Show up five minutes early, park out front to display your vehicle, have brochure and business card ready, review appointment notes before arriving, and double-check the customer's name. When you ring the doorbell, introduce yourself clearly with your company name. Set expectations by explaining the three-step process: walk around together, take measurements and calculate price in your car, then present pricing inside sitting at their table. Use the opening question 'What's the story? What makes now the time to get this done?' to understand their deeper reason and demonstrate genuine listening throughout the consultation.

real_qa.q: Why is the follow-up phone call critical to closing contractor sales and how should it be structured?
real_qa.r: Most contractors give one quote and wait, but following up is a core part of the sales process. The follow-up call is a second chance to close. Start with genuine intentions and have the proposal details in front of you. Rebuild value first by recapping the project scope, answer embarrassed questions they didn't ask during the estimate, explain your process, and highlight what separates you. Only after rebuilding value and creating genuine excitement do you mention any discount. The discount is the cherry on top, not the main selling point.
real_qa.requete: contractor follow-up phone call sales technique

real_qa.q: What are the five unspoken questions running through a customer's mind during a contractor estimate?
real_qa.r: Is this company capable of solving my problem? Can I trust them to do a good job? Do they know what they're doing? Does this person match what I experienced before booking? Based on this conversation, will they be out of my budget? These five questions are subconscious and must be answered through your actions and approach during the walkthrough, or it becomes very hard for the customer to focus on what you're saying.

real_qa.q: How should contractors use instant value responses to overcome customer objections during estimates?
real_qa.r: You should know every common reason someone hires you and have a specific value response prepared for each. If a customer mentions selling their house, respond with 'We handle these all the time' or offer specific solutions. If they mention wood rot, say 'We have a carpenter on staff.' For HOA concerns, offer 'We'll email the HOA to let them know you've hired us, which usually buys you more time.' These instant responses show expertise and should be prepared in advance so you can respond naturally instead of reading from a script.
